article.story: CHICAGO -- — Jeffery Simmons delivered once again. That blockbuster trade for the All-Pro defensive tackle is looking like the appropriate price at the moment. Simmons had three of Chicago's six sacks, Caleb Williams threw two touchdown passes and the Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13 on Sunday for their fifth consecutive win. Led by Simmons and Montez Sweat — who also played together in college at Mississippi State — Chicago’s defense made a handful of big plays on a sluggish day for Williams and the offense. Sweat got a safety when he sacked Tyler Shough in the end zone with 12:55 left. Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman had an interception, and Austin Booker recovered a fumble. “I couldn’t be more proud of our defensive effort here today,” coach Ben Johnson said. “I thought those guys played their tails off really for the whole 60 minutes. A ton of sacks throughout. Multiple turnovers that turned into points for us.” Chicago sent three draft picks — including two first-round selections — to Tennessee for Simmons and a fifth-round pick on Oct. 29. It was a bold move by general manager Ryan Poles, the kind that will be connected to his name for a long time, and the early returns have been better than anyone on the Bears could have reasonably expected. Simmons has five sacks in three games with his new team. He got to Shough on New Orleans' first drive and pulled him down again in the final minute of the first half. He matched his career high when he slung Shough to the ground late in the fourth quarter. “For me as I learned as I got older and matured in this league, it’s just own that moment,” Simmons said. “I know this team brought me in here and they expect me to win my one-on-ones and I expect to take full advantage of them.” Williams was 15 for 23 for 181 yards in his first game since he threw a career-high four interceptions in a 27-24 win over Tampa Bay on Nov. 8. Chicago (8-2) was off last weekend for its bye. Playing without offensive linemen Taliese Fuaga and Erik McCoy because of injuries, New Orleans (3-7) lost for the third time in four games. Shough was 25 for 42 for 222 yards. Chris Olave had nine receptions for 102 yards. “That game wasn’t without the opportunities to make some plays, and we just didn’t get it done,” New Orleans coach Kellen Moore said. New Orleans scored one touchdown on seven drives that ended in Chicago territory. Charlie Smyth missed a 47-yard field goal late in the first half. Trailing 21-10 in the fourth, the Saints turned the ball over on downs at the Bears 10. “There’s a few minute details on certain plays that have cost us,” Shough said. “And that’s really what it comes down to. It’s frustrating, for sure.” Chicago opened a 10-0 lead on Williams' shovel pass to D'Andre Swift for a 3-yard touchdown with 11:34 left in the first half. A hustling Booker set up the TD when he jumped on a fumble by CJ Donaldson after a 3-yard reception. Shough was picked off by Thieneman on the Saints' next drive, and Williams passed to Colston Loveland for a 15-yard TD with 7:21 to go. Loveland hurdled Julian Blackmon on his way to the end zone, sending a charge through the crowd of 59,911 at Soldier Field. “I got a great view of it,” Williams said. “It was pretty cool to be able to see him go up and make a play for the team.” Loveland said he talked to Blackmon after the game. “He said, ‘Man why’d you have to do me like that?’” a smiling Loveland recounted. New Orleans rallied late in the first half. Alvin Kamara caught a 1-yard touchdown pass on fourth down and Smyth kicked a 56-yard field goal, making it 16-10 at the break. Smyth connected from 51 yards with 1:10 left in the game, but Luther Burden recovered the onside kick for Chicago. Inconsistent day for Chicago's offense Williams was picked off by Danny Stutsman on a deflected ball late in the first half. It was Stutsman's first career interception. Williams said he thinks Chicago's offense can play a lot better. “I think there was opportunity for a lot of points out there, whether it’s us being on the same page, us being efficient running and efficient passing,” he said. “I think there was a lot more we left out there and a lot more we can be better at this week coming up.” Injuries Saints: TE Juwan Johnson had a hamstring injury. Bears: RB Roschon Johnson left in the first quarter with an ankle injury. Up next Saints: at Cincinnati next Sunday. Bears: at Detroit on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
